stem:
The diagram shows lines $PQ$ and $RS$ cut by transversal $AC$. Triangles $PAC$ and $RCA$ are congruent, and that congruence makes one pair of alternate interior angles equal.

Which claim correctly concludes that $PQ \parallel RS$?

options.text: $PQ \parallel RS$, because the congruent triangles make a pair of alternate interior angles equal for transversal $AC$.
Lines $PQ$ and $RS$ are the alternate interior angles on transversal $AC$.
$PQ \parallel RS$, because the triangles are congruent, even when those alternate interior angles are unequal.
$PQ \parallel RS$, because matching sides of the triangles are equal, and equal sides alone settle parallelism.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal alternate interior angles from the congruence force $PQ\parallel RS$. Renaming the lines as the angles swaps terms. Dropping the equal-angle step, or treating equal sides alone as enough, misses the parallel hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as lines PQ and RS cut by transversal AC.
